function.description: Send a GET request to a specified URL to retrieve all products and branches with triangulation runs in the latest 90 days. Note that the provided function is in Python 3 syntax.

url.description: The URL to send the GET request to.

Content-Type.description: The MIME type of the body of the request (used with POST and PUT requests).

Accept.description: The MIME types that are acceptable for the response.

headers.description: Headers to include in the request as a dictionary of header names to header values.

timeout.description: The maximum time in seconds to wait for the server to send data before giving up. This is a float type value.

days.description: The number of days to look back for triangulation runs.

end_date.description: The end date for the data retrieval period, in the format 'YYYY-MM-DD'. If null, defaults to the current date.

params.description: Optional query parameters to include in the request.

auth.description: HTTP authentication credentials as a (username, password) tuple.

cert.description: Path to a certificate file to verify the peer.

cookies.description: Cookies to send with the request as a dictionary of cookie names to cookie values.

http.description: URL of the proxy for HTTP requests.

https.description: URL of the proxy for HTTPS requests.

proxies.description: Proxy settings as a dictionary mapping protocol names to URLs of the proxies.

stream.description: If true, the response should be streamed; otherwise, the response will be downloaded immediately.

verify.description: Whether to verify the server's TLS certificate or not.

message.content:
Triangulation metrics are quantitative measures used to evaluate the accuracy, precision, and reliability of triangulation processes—typically in contexts like geospatial mapping, photogrammetry, or sensor fusion. They help determine how well a set of observations (e.g., images, GPS points, LiDAR scans) can be combined to reconstruct a 3D point or estimate a position.

Key aspects of triangulation metrics include:

| Metric | What it Measures | Typical Use |
|--------|------------------|-------------|
| **Reprojection Error** | Difference between observed image coordinates and projected coordinates from the estimated 3D point. | Assesses how well the estimated geometry fits the data. |
| **Residual Sum of Squares (RSS)** | Aggregate squared differences across all observations. | Provides a single goodness‑of‑fit score. |
| **Root Mean Square Error (RMSE)** | Square root of mean squared residuals. | Normalizes RSS to the same units as the measurements. |
| **Mean Absolute Error (MAE)** | Average absolute difference between observed and predicted values. | Robust to outliers compared to RMSE. |
| **Confidence Intervals / Standard Deviation** | Statistical spread of the estimated point positions. | Indicates uncertainty in the reconstruction. |
| **Covariance Matrix** | Full covariance of the estimated parameters. | Enables propagation of uncertainties into downstream analyses. |
| **Number of Observations / Redundancy** | Count of independent data points contributing to each estimate. | Higher redundancy generally improves robustness. |
| **Outlier Detection Metrics** (e.g., Z‑score, Mahalanobis distance) | Identify anomalous observations that may bias results. | Helps clean data before triangulation. |

In practice, software packages that perform triangulation (e.g., Structure‑from‑Motion pipelines, SLAM systems, or multi‑sensor fusion frameworks) output these metrics so users can assess whether the reconstructed points meet required tolerances or if additional data collection is needed.
